'''Rakesh Kumar Popli''' (1952 &ndash; 15 September 2007) was an Indian [[nuclear physicist]] who would establish the first [[Ekal Vidyalaya]]s, or One-Teacher Schools, in remote regions of India.<ref name=Ekalobit/>

==Early years==
Rakesh Popli was born in India in 1952.

He studied in the United States at [[Purdue University]], from 1974 to 1981, obtaining his doctorate in nuclear physics.

Returning to India, he was accepted as an assistant professor of nuclear physics at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]]. He would later be appointed as a professor of applied physics at the [[Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra]] (BIT Mesra) in [[Ranchi]], Jharkhand, from 1984 to 1988.<ref name=Ekalobit/>

==Ekal vidyalayas==
In 1986, following in the footsteps of the early followers of [[Swami Vivekananda]], some young [[educationist]]s began to work with tribal people who lived in the dense forests of [[Jharkhand]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://www.sanghparivar.org/wiki/ekal-vidyalaya
 |title=Ekal Vidyalaya
 |publisher=[[Sangh Parivar]]
 |access-date=2012-03-22}}</ref>
Sri Bhao Rao Devras had outlined the concept of One Teacher Schools in 1986.<ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://www.ftsindia.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=59&Itemid=68
 |title=AN EKAL VIDYALAYA
 |publisher=[[Friends of Tribals Society]]
 |access-date=2012-03-22}}</ref>
Rakesh Popli and his wife Rama Popli, an expert in child education, then refined the concept.
He wrote the syllabus for the pioneering schools that were established among the tribes of [[Gumla]], about {{convert|125|km|mi}} away from BIT Mesra.<ref name=Ekalobit/>
Sponsored by the India Development Service, a charity, in July/August 1986, Rakesh Popli visited about twenty cities in the United States where he described the work of his group in the tribal areas.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.idsusa.org/IDS1986.pdf
 |title=India Development Service Annual Report - 1986
 |access-date=2012-03-22}}</ref>

Rakesh Popli died from blood cancer on September 15, 2007 after a protracted illness.<ref name=Ekalobit/>
His books included ''A Stroll Through Space Time'' (in Hindi).<ref>{{cite web 
 |url=http://www.vigyanprasar.gov.in/annualreport/ENGLISH.pdf
 |title=VIGYAN PRASAR ANNUAL REPORT 2004-2005
 |access-date=2012-03-22}}</ref>
